text:
mike_h: heads up — p99 tail spiked in prod right after the kernel-selector rollout (around 02:10Z). noticed lots of redispatch events around the same time.
perf-bot: automated alert: p95=130ms p99=420ms (baseline p99 ~140ms). kv-cache hit rate 78% -> 63% on affected fleet. stack: kernel-v2 fallback -> kernel-cold -> redispatch queue.
sara_k: do we have a small trace sample? link? :eyes:
mike_h: https://kibana/reports/trace/246891 — key snippet shows requests that miss KV, hit cold kernels, then get pushed back into continuous-batcher queue and land in larger microbatches, increasing latency tail.
lina_p: that matches what we saw in canary last week. Kernel handoffs + big packet sizes are deadly for p99. I'm thinking two levers: limit max_batch_tokens for redispatched items OR route redispatched to a fast-path kernel that doesn't do heavy fused init.
nate_r: quick experiment idea: mark redispatches with metadata and set a separate scheduler profile with max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=6, prefer_kernel=fast-small. minimal change.
mike_h: agree. also try toggling aggressive KV prefetch for those tokens (prefetch 2 next layers) — might raise CPU but reduce cold hits.
sara_k: small config snippet to test on staging:
```
scheduler.profiles.redispatch = {
  max_batch_tokens: 2048,
  max_wait_ms: 6,
  prefer_kernel: "kernel-fast-path",
  kv_prefetch_layers: 2
}
```
perf-bot: running quick microbenchmark on staging with that profile now.
perf-bot: microbench results (staging snapshot): baseline vs redispatch-profile
  - baseline: p95=120ms p99=430ms q95=1.8x
  - redispatch-profile: p95=125ms p99=165ms q95=1.05x
mike_h: wow p99 improvement is significant, p95 slightly up, throughput dip small. need to see cost impact (tokens/sec down a bit) and regression windows.
lina_p: if redispatch-profile pushes more microbatches we risk throughput loss under high QPS. but it's acceptable for customer-facing strict SLOs.
sara_k: can we run a 30m soak on a subset of prod (10%) and capture tail heatmap + KV hit rate? i'll schedule.
perf-bot: soak scheduled on fleet:prod-redispatch-10pct at 02:45Z for 30m.
perf-bot: mid-soak snapshot (10m): p95=128ms p99=172ms kv-hit=77% cpu+gpu util unchanged.
nate_r: can we also try flipping the other axis: increase max_batch_tokens but reduce max_wait_ms (e.g., tokens=4096, wait=3ms) so microbatches are larger but wait small — tradeoff might reduce throughput variance.
mike_h: yes run that as experiment B concurrently on a different 10% shard. label it "wide-fast".
sara_k: running both A(redispatch-profile) and B(wide-fast) in parallel. will post results.
perf-bot: experiment B (wide-fast) results after 20m: p95=118ms p99=298ms kv-hit=71% throughput +6%.
lina_p: B helps throughput but still higher p99 than A. suggests redispatch-induced cold kernel fallbacks are main tail driver; batching shape matters but kernel choice + prefetch are larger factor.
mike_h: proposed rollout plan: stage A on 25% for 1h, monitor p99 and error rates. if stable, scale to 75% and keep B as fallback for heavy-throughput routes.
sara_k: added canary playbook steps, alerts for p99>250ms and error-rate delta >0.2%. also added quick revert script:
```
# revert
curl -X POST $ADMIN/scheduler/profiles/reset?profile=redispatch
```
nate_r: note: need to update observability to tag redispatched requests so traces show which profile applied. otherwise postmortem will be messy.
mike_h: good call. I'll add tagging in the scheduler header: X-Sched-Profile=redispatch|wide-fast|baseline.
perf-bot: final note from soak: A reduces p99 by ~60% with small throughput cost. B increases throughput but only partial p99 relief. recommend A for interactive routes and B for background/high-throughput endpoints.
lina_p: fine-grained rollout tomorrow. i'll own observability changes + kernel fallback telemetry.
sara_k: thanks all. follow-up: schedule a perf retro 3pm PST to decide permanent defaults and cost tradeoffs. :calendar:
mike_h: ack, will bring heatmaps + kv-hit time series.
